_comment: The NON-BANK base profile (rc.26). Until now `regulated-bank` was the only base, which made the floor of the profile system a bank: a team building software with AI under ordinary engineering discipline had to adopt a bank's approver set to adopt anything. That is a positioning accident, not a design decision — the warp (four-eyes merge, the waist gate, spec-first, quality gates, no self-merge) is what makes the method work, and none of it is banking-specific. This profile is that warp and nothing more. Requirements are CUMULATIVE by tier: the compiler unions everything at or below the envelope's tier, so higher tiers only add. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: PA1/PA2 product approval, the A-series architecture assurance, R-series operational readiness, second-line hold, external anchoring, and every control-function approver role. Those are not 'advanced' — they are what a REGULATED institution owes its regulator, and asserting them here would be the same overstatement this method exists to refuse. If you are a regulated entity, use `regulated-bank`; it is a strictly stronger profile, not a different one. ADOPT: tighten to your policy; you cannot loosen a lower tier from a higher one. INVARIANT, asserted by profiles.test.mjs: at every tier `standard` requires a SUBSET of what `regulated-bank` requires. If it ever required something the bank profile does not, a regulated adopter would miss a control an unregulated one gets — which is incoherent, and the fastest way to make the profile system untrustworthy. Add to regulated-bank first, then here.
